current.text: Experts project him to start in Boston over Payton Pritchard. One expert is only about 45% sure of it.
Even as a starter, he is expected to play only about 20 to 22 minutes.
Boston is very deep, with at least 12 rotation-level players. Pritchard, Hauser, Robinson, Walsh and Conley are projected off the bench.
Jayson Tatum and Paul George replace Jaylen Brown. Experts say this leaves less usage for Boston's guards.
In his last 8 games as a starter last season, he played 23 minutes a night and averaged 10 points, 2.5 threes, 3 rebounds and 2.5 assists. He shot 47% from the field and did not miss a free throw.
He is a name to watch in his third season. He could reach double-digit scoring with more catch-and-shoot looks.
He is an interesting late flier and a late swing pick for deeper leagues. One expert has him barely inside the top 300.
Boston plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. That is one game short of the maximum.

durable.text: He can shoot and pass, is not a bad defender, and is bigger than Pritchard.

note: Both sites give him 0 USD (rank 213 on ESPN, 296 on Yahoo), so he falls outside the 144 players drafted in our league. Do not draft him. Put him on the waiver watch list for the first weeks. Even ESPN's projection of 25 minutes only gets him to 7.5 points with few blocks. His 89% FT% comes on under 1 attempt a game, so it barely moves the team ratio. Check early whether he starts over Pritchard and plays 23 or more minutes, like in his 8-game starting stretch (10 points, 2.5 threes). If he does, he becomes a cheap add for 3PM and low turnovers.
